items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024

ctx.x: Chaucer. Chaucer. But he also was not playing “Lady of Spain” he was one of the first to get those — all those new-fangled things that the accordions were able to do — yeah, like a computer. Almost like an electric piano. So he had one of those and he wasn’t a jazz player but he could play really good harmony on the accordion and that’s what I got used to, singing. And later on my father encouraged me to accompany myself and sing with myself. So I had both.
Do you think you accompany significantly differently when you accompany another singer?
